pageCache.pageTitle: A Thinking School | Prep School London | Notting Hill Prep
pageCache.text:
A Thinking School
Promoting academic excellence while protecting the joy of childhood.
GIVING SPACE TO GROW
BECAUSE Community Matters
WHAT OTHERS SAY ABOUT NHP
It’s a true sign of an ‘incredible’ school when children ‘cry if they have to take the day off’– and that’s as much to do with Notting Hill Prep’s ‘warm and loving environment’ as it is its unique way of ‘cultivating curiosity and a love of learning’, without compromising on academic results.
Full of energy and happiness, NHP is unique. Its philosophy won’t align with everyone, but from those it does, the message is clear. ‘We are so lucky to be part of the warmest, smartest, most interesting, silliest, most energetic and fun school there is,’ says one parent. ‘The children say NHP stands for No Happier Place – and that’s pretty much spot on.’
Impressive and creative. Underpinning the curriculum are De Bono’s thinking hats. These metacognitive tools encourage the kids to learn problem solving and critical thinking from a young age. Add the school’s four values – wonder, challenge, self-knowledge and community – into the mix and you get a teaching style that encourages pupils to deep dive into topics, consider wider implications and ask lots of questions.
You won’t find many schools that nurture children’s minds by following the principles of Edward de Bono’s theory of Six Thinking Hats, but Notting Hill Prep likes to do things differently….Head Maxine Scully…is committed to the prep’s Thinking School status, believing it creates academic rigour while preserving the joy of childhood. It’s certainly no slouch on academics, with pupils leaving for the likes of Westminster, Eton and St Paul’s Girls.
Life skills and mindfulness are just as important as passing exams – but these pupils are certainly no slouches on that front. Specialist teachers make learning fun, with loads of practical activities like ‘kung-fu maths’ and hands-on science experiments in the school’s superlabs. Everyone is prepped for 11+, when a few girls peel off to London day schools; the rest stay on till 13 and bag places at top spots including The Harrodian, Bradfield, Francis Holland and Brighton College.
…slap bang in the middle of the hustle and bustle of W11 life, although once inside things are very different. Notting Hill Prep (NHP) is in a soundproofed bubble with a state-of-the-art air-filtration system, resident hens, rooftop beehives, and a woodland style adventure playground. When you add in the small class sizes – capped at 22, rather fabulous.

pageCache.pageTitle: About Us | Prep School Notting Hill | Notting Hill Prep
pageCache.text:
About Notting Hill Prep
Notting Hill Prep is a co-educational independent preparatory school situated in Notting Hill in the west of London. Catering for children aged 4-13 we combine a comprehensive academic curriculum with our core value of preserving the joy of childhood.
Our approach to teaching prioritises developing how children consider and absorb learning rather than just what they know. Our head teacher Maxine Scully is passionate about guiding pupils to become confident and independent in their educational journey and beyond – not just how to sit an exam!
From their first day in reception to their final year at NHP, pupils are recognised as individuals. Small classes, committed form tutors and a diverse curriculum mean no child gets lost in the crowd, be that academically or personally.
School at a Glance
Co-educational independent preparatory school
Notting Hill, London
Advanced Accredited Thinking School, University of Exeter
Senior School Pathways
Leading day and boarding schools (Harrodian, Regents Park, Harrow)
Our Approach to Teaching
NHP is officially an Advanced Accredited Thinking School, certified by the University of Exeter, we focusjust as much on how children approach obstacles as teaching them what the curriculum requires. Cognitive learning strategies are part of our philosophy and applied into everyday school life, in every subject from science to the arts.
This means that students are encouraged to explain their thought processes as well as challenge their own assumptions, working through obstacles rather than simply reaching for an answer. Through their journey with us they will build resilience and analytical thinking that will serve them for the rest of their lives.
Curriculum & Pastoral Care
Pupils follow a broad and comprehensive curriculum all the way from reception to 13+. They are taught by subject specialists the whole way through the school. In line with core subjects, music, art, sport and drama are treated as essential to a well rounded education, and not as extras.
Every child at NHP has a form tutor who they will get to know during their time with us. They are familiar with students academically, socially and personally, helping them to feel happy and secure. Students do their best work when they are comfortable in their environment and that is why pastoral care is such an important part of life at NHP, underpinning everything we do.
Frequently Asked Questions
Is Notting Hill Prep co-educational?
Yes. NHP is a fully co-educational independent preparatory school, welcoming students of all genders through all years.
What age can children join Notting Hill Prep?
NHP accepts children from the ages of 4-13 with entry points at reception 7+ and 11+. You can visit our admissions page for more information on how and when to apply.
What curriculum does NHP follow?
NHP follows a diverse and academically comprehensive curriculum taught by specialists in their field. Alongside traditional core subjects we have a strong offering in music, sport, art and drama. You can find more information on our curriculum page.
What makes NHP different from other London prep schools?
As an Advanced Accredited Thinking School, NHP applies cognitive learning strategies into everyday school life. Helping our pupils to develop into resilient, independent thinkers rather than simply strong exam candidates.
How do I apply to Notting Hill Prep?
The best place to start is by booking a place on one of our Open Days. Or visit our admissions page for more information on key dates and the application process.

pageCache.pageTitle: Head's Welcome | Prep School London | Notting Hill Prep
pageCache.text:
As a mother of three children, I remember how daunting it was choosing the ‘right’ school for them. How on earth did I know what sort of child they would be by the time they were four, especially as number three hadn’t appeared as the decision was being made! Unlike senior school, where you should very much base your decision upon your child’s ability, personality and interests, prep school is more of a decision guided by your heart as a parent.
In London you are spoilt for choice, and the options are all very good schools. They provide brilliant education in small classes with amazing co-curriculum programmes. Do you dust off the crystal ball then to help you make that choice? My advice to you is to spend some time visiting schools and getting a feel for them. There will be something, intangible, which helps you to decide which school will make your child the happiest. When they are happy, they will engage fully and work harder which, in turn, will lead to better results.
I am delighted to be leading Notting Hill Prep. I have worked in many different schools, and I can genuinely say none of them have been anything like NHP. We have a brilliant staff team, we have supportive parents and we have simply brilliant children who refer to NHP as ‘no happier place’. But it is the culture within the school that makes it so very special. The ‘Thinking School’ approach is fully embedded and it is tangible when you talk to the children. They know how to learn as well as what they need to learn. They can tell you why their learning is relevant and how they can use their skills and knowledge to develop further in other academic areas. They ask as many questions as they answer and are in control of their learning. It is very special to experience.
“When children are happy, they will engage fully and work harder which, in turn, will lead to better results”

pageCache.pageTitle: NHP Ethos | Prep School London | Notting Hill Prep
pageCache.text:
Academic excellence + a joy of childhood = NHP
Notting Hill Prep was founded in 2003 under Headmistress, Jane Cameron, with the vision of creating a local co-educational prep school, with strong partnerships between the school and the parents. NHP began with two important school rules, that still hold true today; every child should have the right to come to school each day feeling safe and happy.
Establishing a brand-new school was truly exciting and allowed NHP to set its own parameters for curriculum design and learning, using the very best ideas from educational research and practice, both past and present. This determination to ensure that the education we provide for our children is based upon worldwide best practice is as strong today as it was in 2003. The learning is dynamic and exciting and ensures excellent progress for the pupils.
We also continue to strengthen our belief in traditional values and teach the children to have a strong moral compass, to recognise the need for hard work in all areas of school life and to appreciate that the privilege of a good education brings with it the responsibility to give back. We expect our pupils to be thoroughly decent human beings.
Underpinning an NHP education is a fundamental belief in academic excellence, coupled with a recognition that childhood is both short and precious. In a rapidly changing and pressurised world, it is vital that we cherish and protect our pupils’ childhoods and ensure that they are filled with joy.
Our aim is to educate our children in the truest sense of the word and the following two quotes epitomise what we aim to do.
This culture of active learning is led by dynamic and inspiring teachers and driven by our Thinking School approach, we strive to develop a passion for learning and a strong sense of self that will carry our pupils through their school years and beyond.
At the heart of an NHP education are four key values:
WONDER
We are curious. We know that a question is almost always the first stage in both the learning process and in finding our voice and so we encourage them. We inspire debate and seek intellectual growth. We find joy in imagination, passion, adventure and original thought and we nurture those qualities in our pupils.
CHALLENGE
We are ambitious. We believe that a child’s school years should be a time when they feel safe to challenge and be challenged. When children do not fear failure, they are ready to express their own views, test out new ideas and take risks. At NHP, we celebrate being out of our comfort zone both personally and academically. We see making mistakes, and learning from them, as the path to deeper learning.
SELF-KNOWLEDGE
We think about ourselves. We encourage our pupils to be aware of what they think and feel in certain situations. Observing our own actions and reactions is the first step towards being more conscious of how we learn, how we behave and who we are. Increased self-knowledge is a key part of future success and growing into the person you would like to be.
COMMUNITY
We think about others. We take time to observe and consider the lives and needs of the people around us. We are part of many different communities: cultural, social, local, national and international. Appreciating the diversity and complexity of other people deepens our ability to empathise. We advocate that whilst you are forging your own path you have a responsibility to look after and respect others along the way. In short, we encourage the children to be the best person they can be. You will know an NHP pupil, not by what makes them the same, but by what makes them stand out from the crowd.

pageCache.pageTitle: Radius Community Partnerships | Notting Hill Prep School
pageCache.text:
Radius
Radius is our community partnerships programme. We work closely with a number of local primary schools and charitable organisations, with a focus on improving and enriching the lives of primary-school aged children.
Through Radius we identify and support community-based endeavours that align with NHP’s core values. With the support of the Parents’ Association, the Foundation aims to provide both financial assistance and to share resources with the wider community through project funding and running regular events with local primary schools and organisations.
We believe all pupils mutually benefit from these partnerships, developing a motivation to help and raise awareness of the needs of others from an early age. Through striving to create a school environment that more closely represents the diversity of our local area, we offer a richer and more meaningful educational experience for all students involved.
Since its launch in 2020, the NHP community has raised over £70,000 for Radius projects, reaching over 1000 students and a number of local schools and organisations. Each year, we hope to be able to support a larger project through funding a specific area of need within a local school or charitable organisation.
Radius is able to provide financial assistance to projects in the region of £3,000-£5,000. If you have a local charity in mind who needs our support, or a local project focussed on improving and enriching the lives of local primary school aged children, we would love to hear from you! Please contact our Head of Development, Sarah Clark, sclark@nottinghillprep.com
donate to our Radius Programme
Current Projects 2025/26
Care to Grow Mentor Programme
Care to Grow exists to emotionally support children to help them learn and thrive. They are a team of child mental health practitioners working at a range of levels of expertise in order to provide high quality and good value sessional work within schools. They have partnership agreements with schools to identify the most in need or at-risk children who could benefit from a session a week with a dedicated adult. They work solely within North Kensington as the work there (whilst they were a community group from late 2023 onwards, before registering as a charity), showed the chronic level of need in that area, especially in response to Grenfell.
From September 2025, the NHP Foundation will be funding Care to Grow’s “mentor scheme” for St Francis of Assisi. St Francis of Assisi are within very close proximity to Grenfell Tower and have a number of children who were impacted directly by the devastating fire. This scheme, which will run from September 2025-July 2026, will coincide with the demolition of the tower. 5 children per term will be allocated to have sessions, meaning 15 children who need it the most will benefit from these sessions per year.
The Notting Hill Children's Community Choir
The NHCCC is a weekly community choir based on fun, not ability, which we launched in 2021 for eight participating local primary schools, including NHP. Up to 48 children meet each week at the Notting Hill Methodist Church to have fun, sing together and enjoy working with other schools.
We are currently working with Saint Francis of Assisi Catholic Primary, Oxford Gardens Primary, Colville Primary, St Mary’s Primary, Thomas Jones Primary, Avondale Park Primary and St Charles Primary.
“The best thing about choir for me is making new friends from different schools. Our confidence grew more too because we realised the atmosphere was just so friendly.” NHCCC member
Avondale Park Primary Weekly PE lessons - Year 6
Thanks to the amazing support received from our NHP community, we pleased to be able to fund another term of weekly PE lessons at Avondale Park Primary, this time for their Year 6’s!
Previous Projects
Avondale Park Primary Weekly PE lessons - Year 5
For the Spring and Summer Terms, 2025, we supported the provision of a weekly PE lesson for Year 6 pupils at Avondale Park Primary School. Avondale was struggling to afford this essential part of every child’s development themselves and we are delighted to be able to help.
“Thank you so much for arranging this. The Netball is going really well and my class especially have improved lots and are showing good progress. The children have learnt so much and are really enjoying their PE” – Avondale Park Primary School
St Francis of Assisi Weekly Drama Club
We are funding a weekly Drama club at St Francis of Assisi Primary for the Summer term. Drama is a vital tool to enable children to express themselves in a safe space, something St Francis have seen have a hugely positive impact on their pupils. We are delighted to enable the provision of this free club for St Francis of Assisi pupils to continue for another term.
“Teachers have observed that drama club has helped with confidence, engagement and also reduced absenteeism in some persistent cases. We are thrilled to be able to offer this high quality learning experience to the children at school who would otherwise never be able to access this club. Thank you so much to all of you at NHP Radius for brightening our summer term and allowing our children such an enriching experience!” – St Francis of Assisi Primary
“We want to broaden Children’s horizons and ambitions. We want them to feel that regardless of their circumstances and financial constraints that they too can express themselves creatively and confidently” – St Francis of Assisi Primary
The Family Group - Avondale Park Primary
Through our Radius Partnerships Programme, we worked with Avondale Park Primary to part-fund The Family Group, a group therapy model delivered weekly to 8 families with children in Years 2 and 3. The sessions promote wellbeing and learning for children struggling socially, emotionally, behaviourally or academically over an 18 month period. The sessions allow for parents to share in a non-judgmental environment as well as form a strong support network between group members. The cost of this programme is £26,000 per year, of which Radius contributed £13,000 in the 2023-24 academic year.
The Children's Book Project
The Children’s Book Project re-home pre-loved books. In Autumn 2023, we donated over 1000 books, all of which fell into the hands of children who need them the most.
The Harrow Club
We worked closely with The Harrow Club which shares our vision of a society where all children and young people, regardless of background, can grow and fulfil their potential in a safe and supportive community. Founded in 1883, they work with some of the most marginalised young people in West London to provide accessible and high-quality opportunities, enabling them to maximise their life chances and to enhance their personal development. We will be partnering with them to support on the delivery of their Junior Programme, often a last resort for children aged 8-12 who are at serious risk of being excluded from their schools.
Approximately 70 children benefit from the opportunity to attend two afternoon sessions a week during term time, taking part in a variety of sports and educational projects encompassing music, arts and crafts, dance, drama, cookery and a homework club. The objectives are to improve confidence, communication skills and well-being, as well as teaching specific skills. The cost of running this programme is around £16,000 a year. Due to recent cuts in funding, they are currently running just one weekly session using limited funds from their reserves. Through our partnership, we raised £8,000 of vital funds to offer their second weekly session for a year – a lifeline for so many children.
Rise Kids
RISE Kids was brought to our attention by Young K&C, a charity that works with partner organisations to support vulnerable children in the local area. RISE Kids was initially set up by local parents to support children and families who have been affected by the Grenfell fire, RISE Kids hold vital summer camps for local children in need who have been worst affected by the pandemic over the past year. These camps are a lifeline for low income families in the local area, offering activities to help children learn and develop their knowledge and skills, whilst having fun and seeing friends. During Summer 2021, they ran a holiday programme for over 100 children.
Thanks to the support from NHP, we raised £5,343.75 for RISE Kids, which was then match funded by a £5,000 grant from Young K&C. This not only allowed them to offer a four-week programme of arts, cultural activities and sports for the children and the opportunity to visit places like the Natural History Museum and the Design Museum but to also run another activity camp in the October half term.
Avondale Extra
A charity founded in 2002 by local volunteers to benefit the children of Avondale Park Primary School. Their aim is to broaden experience and create lifelong interests in their pupils through funding activities (including sports, the arts, educational excursions and residential trips) and providing resources that make a significant difference to their lives. 44% of the students at Avondale Park, who attend school less than a mile away from NHP, are eligible for free school meals, compared to the national average of 13.7%. The Covid-19 pandemic has hit a number of these families particularly hard. The closure of schools has meant a lack of regular meals for many children, as well as difficulty accessing technology for remote learning. Avondale Extra is helping to bridge that gap by enabling access to vital educational resources such as laptops, providing after school provision, and a breakfast club run by teaching staff.
Almost £23,000 was raised by the NHP community in support of this fantastic initiative.

Leavers’ Destinations
NHP pupils leave us at either 11 or 13 to both day and boarding schools. Just as there is no ‘typical’ NHP pupil, our pupils go on to a wide range of senior schools, both in London and further afield. Here at NHP we work closely with parents to offer a bespoke service which ensures that we find the right next school for every child.
2025 Offers
We are thrilled to celebrate an exceptional set of outcomes for our Year 6 pupils, who have received offers from many of London’s most sought-after independent schools and leading UK boarding schools. These results reflect not only the hard work and ambition of our pupils, but also the curiosity, confidence and individuality nurtured throughout their time at NHP. From 196 senior school applications that progressed to interview, an impressive 163 resulted in offers or waitlist places — a testament to the character, charm, and thoughtfulness of our pupils as conversationalists and young thinkers.
Leavers continue to head to a diverse range of schools, with many now deferring to 13+ rather than leaving at 11+, reflecting strong offers from both top London day schools and leading boarding schools.

We are particularly proud of the thirteen scholarships awarded this year, across academic, creative and all-round disciplines — celebrating the breadth of talent across our cohort. Pupils also secured offers from highly selective schools such as Latymer Upper, UCS, Westminster and Radley.
These outcomes speak to the core values we hold at NHP: wonder, challenge, self-knowledge, and community. Our pupils step forward not just with impressive results, but with a strong sense of who they are and how they want to shape the world around them. We could not be prouder of them.

pageCache.text:
NAVIGATING 11+ and 13+
There are two official exit points from NHP: end of Year 6 (11+) and end of Year 8 (13+).
13+ is the more traditional prep school exit route. Joining a senior school in Year 9 can be a great option for:
The admissions process for the majority of schools listed above requires pupils to sit the ISEB Common Pre-Test in the autumn term of Year 6. Most pupils entering Year 7 at NHP will have already secured their place at a senior school of their choice. On a select basis, schools offer NHP pupils an alternative assessment in Year 7 or 8 for late joiners.
Generally, the entry process for 13+ can feel more holistic. Greater time and emphasis are placed on the interview and assessing the child as a whole, versus leaping the academic hurdle of 11+. The Common Entrance syllabus expects all-round attainment in a wide range of subjects but is no longer a condition of entry to many schools.
leavers destinations
“I’m a firm believer in the beauty of a prep school education up to Year 8 – you can develop socially in those potentially tricky early teenage years and be pushed academically by teachers who know you well, care about you, and will support you with a successful transition to your next school. Years 7 and 8 allow children to be children just that little bit longer.”
“The power of being role-models to younger pupils without the influences of older teenagers must not be underestimated. NHP pupils come to Wellington with an unbelievable energy, bringing top values to all aspects of school life and are often the kind and empathetic ‘glue’ in the centre of their house groups.”
“There are undoubted benefits to staying on in your prep school for Years 7 and 8. Pupils enjoy being at the top of their school and the opportunities that are open to them at this stage. Important senior positions allow them to assume responsibility, whilst they are encouraged to become increasingly independent and cultivate their resilience. This in turn builds confidence as they start to think about their senior schools.”
those considering boarding
What makes NHP the right choice for your child…
ENVIRONMENT
The Portobello Green Building (PGB), which houses our Years 6 to 8, has a markedly studious air and its own individual identity. It was designed specifically as a senior school environment to mark the pupils’ transition from primary school and mirrors many of the structures that the children will encounter at their next schools. The academic and pastoral needs of each pupil are closely monitored by a dedicated team: the Head of Upper School, the Deputy Head (Pastoral) and the Deputy Head (Academic), assisted by individual Form Teachers. Each of them has an in-depth knowledge of your child and their learning profile.
ACADEMIC
There is a conscious shift of responsibility onto the children for their own independent learning and behaviour. Small classes and sets (approximately 10-18 pupils) are taught exclusively by highly-experienced subject specialists. The previously traditional Common Entrance syllabus has been overhauled by the ISEB (Independent Schools Exam Board) and now represents a more progressive curriculum framework. NHP offers the IPQ (Independent Project Qualification) as the final assessment in the humanities. Pupils are very well prepared under this system for the academic demands of their senior school including independent, research-based learning, and revision and exam techniques.
PERSONAL GROWTH
For some, the intimacy of the senior years at NHP provides an opportunity to develop a sense of self. Strong self-esteem, both personal and academic, helps greatly in ensuring a successful transition to the additional challenges of senior school.
Our pupils are growing up in the heart of a thriving city. The years between 11 and 13 are crucial for developing ‘street smarts’, independence, and resilience. NHP is a safe environment for making mistakes, pushing some boundaries and learning to navigate London.
Although pupil numbers are relatively small, friendships are well established, familiar and supportive. Remaining in co-education helps to encourage a mixed friendship group, especially relevant if the preferred destination is a single-sex school.
There are many opportunities for our senior pupils to take on leadership roles, actively mentor the younger children and represent the all-important NHP pupil voice.
NHP has established its own senior pupil leadership programme, created in the image of the Duke of Edinburgh awards, with various levels of attainment in leadership, service, physical challenge and creativity.
We have an established third-party mentoring programme which allows pupils a regular and safe space to set goals and address specific worries or concerns.

pageCache.pageTitle: Co-Curricular Activities | Notting Hill Prep School
pageCache.text:
At Notting Hill Prep, we believe that a child’s education is about far more than what happens between 8.10 am and 3.15 pm. Our co-curricular programme is a core part of the NHP experience, offering every pupil the chance to discover new passions, build confidence, and develop skills that classroom learning alone cannot provide.
With well over 100 clubs running across the week – spanning sport, the arts, languages, technology and academic enrichment – there is something to spark curiosity in every child, whatever their interests or stage of development.
Why Co-Curricular Activities Matter
Decades of educational research point to the same conclusion: children who take part in a rich mix of extra-curricular activities tend to do better both in and out of the classroom. Our curriculum is excellent, but co-curricular clubs help children to:
How NHP Delivers
Because NHP is a Thinking School with high academic expectations, we place equal importance on giving children the space, time and encouragement to explore beyond the curriculum. Our co-curricular offer is built around a few key principles:
What’s On Offer
Here is a flavour of the huge range of clubs available across a typical week at NHP:
A full, up-to-date list of clubs – including which are open to all pupils and which are by invitation only – is shared with families at the start of each term, as clubs vary term to term according to demand and the school calendar.
Encouraging every child to get involved
We know that trying something new can feel daunting, particularly for younger children or those who are naturally more reserved. Form teachers and club leaders actively encourage pupils to step outside their comfort zone, and our house system and pupil leadership roles (School Council, House Captains, Sports Captains and more) give children further ways to build confidence and take on responsibility beyond the clubs programme itself.
Parents are welcome to speak to their child’s form teacher or the school office about which clubs might suit their child, particularly during their first term at NHP.
Frequently Asked Questions About Our Co-Curricular Clubs
How many co-curricular clubs does NHP offer?
NHP offers well over 100 clubs across the school year, covering sport, music, drama, art, languages, coding, chess and more, with a fresh timetable of options shared with families each term.
Are clubs available to all year groups?
Yes. Clubs are tailored by age and stage, from clubs designed specifically for our youngest pupils in Reception and Year 1 through to more advanced, often invitation-only, groups for pupils in Years 5 to 8.
Do children need any prior experience to join a club?
No. The vast majority of clubs are open to beginners and are designed to introduce children to a new skill or interest, regardless of previous experience.
Are any clubs invitation-only?
A small number of clubs, typically our most advanced music, art and choir groups, are by invitation, offering an extra challenge to pupils who have shown particular aptitude or commitment in those areas.
How do parents find out which clubs are running each term?
A full, confirmed list of clubs is sent to families before the start of each term. Popular clubs can fill up quickly, so early sign-up is recommended.
Is there an extra cost for co-curricular clubs?
Details of any additional costs, where they apply, are set out alongside the termly clubs list; many clubs are included as part of school life at no extra charge. Families can contact the school office for specific pricing information.
Do clubs run every day of the week?
Yes. NHP runs a full programme of lunchtime and after-school clubs from Monday to Friday, giving pupils flexibility to build a weekly timetable around their own interests.

pageCache.text:
Choosing a school for your child is a huge emotional investment. It will shape their future and as parents we want to get it right!
For ease of reference, we have listed some key facts about life at NHP but nothing beats a visit!
NHP is non-selective
We do not assess pupils academically prior to entry into Reception and we are mixed ability throughout the school. Children who join us after Reception are invited to join us for a taster day prior to offers being made, to ensure that they will love being part of the school community.
NHP is co-educational
We believe in boys and girls being educated alongside each other and the benefits that this brings to everyone.
NHP believes in building firm foundations
We work with parents to identify a list of ideal senior schools for your child’s next step either at 11+ (Year 6) or 13+ (Year 8). We do not prepare children for the 7+ or 8+ exams, favouring firm foundations and a breadth of opportunity over exam technique in the early years of education.
NHP has a considered informal style
Starting a school from scratch has allowed us to design a learning environment that is built upon the best research and practice from education, past and present. NHP has a progressive spirit underpinned by traditional values such as the importance of a strong moral compass and a determination to work hard and be the best that you can be. We have high academic expectations but also recognise fully the importance of childhood.
NHP has a very strong sense of community
Working in partnership with our parent body and building strong relationships with the local community are fundamental to our approach.
NHP is a split-site school
The children will journey through three purpose-built buildings during their time here, each with their own distinct character and atmosphere. Pupils transition from the Old Building (Lower School – Reception to Year 2) to the Jane Cameron Building (Middle School – Year 3 to 5) and on into the Portobello Green Building (Upper School – Year 6 to 8).
Staying connected
House system
In order to strengthen the sense of community and generate a healthy understanding of competition the pupils are divided into four houses: Arundel, Blenheim, Elgin and Lansdowne. Children are assigned to a house from Reception and members of a family join the same house. Each house has a pupil House Captain and a member of staff Head of House.
House meetings and inter-house sports competitions are held throughout each term and each pupil strives to gain valuable house points for good behaviour and/or work for the highly coveted annual House Cup. Charity events and fundraisers are organised by the children under the guidance of the Head of House.
Pupil voice
To make sure the children feel heard at every stage of their time with us, we give as many opportunities as possible to our pupils to undertake leadership roles within the school. Some examples of these include: School Council representatives, House Captains, Sports Captains, Ambassadors, Kindness Monitors, Playground Buddies, Prefects and Head Pupil/s.
These roles keep the children connected, help build confidence, resilience, teamwork and understanding of others, as well as teaching the Fundamental British Values of democracy, the rule of law, individual liberty and mutual respect and tolerance.
A note from our Pupil Voice Lead
The new team of Pupil Council representatives has been assembled (with their shiny new badges) and we have already begun responding to the suggestions from our classmates. You asked for brand new football goals- we have given you brand new football goals! Hooray!
I am incredibly excited to work with such a fantastic group of children this year. We are meeting regularly to ensure that the pupil voice is heard, loud and clear. Our next meetings will take place during the first week of December.
-Miss Pardoe (Pupil Voice Lead)

Co-Ed Prep School in London: The Co-Educational Advantage
At Notting Hill Prep, we promote a warm and ambitious environment where students learn together, reflecting the world that they’re growing into. Being a co-educational prep school in London means that we educate all pupils side by side, sharing classrooms, curriculum, activities and school life. All in the heart of Notting Hill, West London.
The purpose of this page is to detail what exactly a co-ed prep school offers and how it compares to single-sex education.
What Is a Co-Ed Prep School?
Co-education is when, during school, boys and girls learn together in the same classroom. Pupils share school life and mix to form a school community not based on gender.
Co-ed and co-education are synonyms. They are not separate programmes or initiatives, it’s just how NHP is structured the whole way through the school.
Why Choose a Co-Educational Prep School in London?
A main draw of a co-educational environment is the reflection of the real world. Boys and girls will go on to work, socialise and live together throughout their lives, so for many children there is no need to separate them at an early age.
A few of the practical reasons families choose this model:
The main benefit of co-education during primary school isn’t necessarily a quantifiable outcome. It’s that it supplies children with consistent practice communicating and working with a mixed group, that mirrors the environment they will grow up in.
The Co-Ed Prep School Advantage at Notting Hill Prep
For families who prefer a co-ed prep school in Notting Hill, Notting Hill Prep offers a comfortable environment where girls and boys can learn, play and grow together. The whole way through school from age 4 to 13.
As a coeducational prep school in Notting Hill, NHP’s mixed learning environment runs through every part of school life — not just the classroom, but form time, clubs, sport, trips, and pastoral care. Set in the heart of West London, NHP combines this co-educational model with the school’s existing academic and pastoral approach, built around community, confidence and curiosity.
The nature of being a coeducational prep school in Notting Hill means our mixed environment runs through every aspect of school life, not just in the classroom.
Find out more about admissions and visiting NHP.
The Social Benefits of Co-Education
Learning alongside the opposite sex presents a range of social benefits that our families value highly
The Academic Benefits of Co-Education
The value of co-education lies less in it outperforming single sex schools, but more in the variety of discussion, experience and ambition that can be gained when girls and boys learn together.
Some benefits of a co-ed classroom include:
Co-Ed vs Single-Sex Prep Schools
This is the main debate surrounding this topic for London parents. The truth is that both single sex and co-educational schools can be excellent. The ‘right’ choice is much more dependent on the needs and personality of the individual child.
Some parents prefer a single sex environment, citing focus and gender specific education as motivators. There are successful schools of both approaches in the local area, showing how difficult a choice it is for local parents.
Co-educational prep school tend to appeal to parents looking for:
Some things to consider when making this decision could be your child’s confidence, personality and learning style. As well as their existing friendships. It really does depend on what suits your child best, no one approach is an automatic fit for every family.
Breaking Down Gender Stereotypes Early
Another benefit of co-ed is the lack of the learning habit that certain subjects, behaviours or activities belong to or are typical of a certain gender.
As girls and boys are presented with the same problems and opportunities alongside each other. They learn that all the subjects are for everyone. As they will see mixed interactions every day, they will be taught that confidence, kindness and sensitivity aren’t gendered traits but qualities that anyone can bring to any part of school life.
What Co-Education Looks Like Day to Day at NHP
Co-education isn’t a USP for Notting Hill Prep, it’s something that is built into our school community.
What the Research Says
The study of the effects of single sex and co-educational schools is a complex and nuanced area. There is not necessarily a ‘better’ model, you as a parent will have to decide which is suited to your child.
Some studies indicate a higher uptake of STEM subjects in girls at single-sex schools. But other more expansive studies point in the other direction, one well known and international analysis found little to no difference between the two once factors like background were stripped away. There are also some studies that suggest that anxiety levels heightened in students at single sex schools that move to co-educational institutions later in their lives.
In plain terms the research is very varied and any source that claims a definitive answer, should be treated with some scepticism.
The argument for co-education extends beyond purely academics, the social and developmental benefits are unmatched, as well as the reflection of how the real-world works. But parents will find it more worthwhile judging the school’s overall culture, pastoral care and level of teaching, not just gender alone. Your main worry should be what is best for your child and that is something only you and your family can resolve.
Is a Co-Ed Prep School Right for Your Child?
A few things to consider while you weigh up your options:
If most of these resonate with you, then a co-ed prep school in London is likely to be an environment in which your child will thrive. The best way to find out is to visit NHP and see for yourself.
Does your child enjoy collaborative learning?
Frequently Asked Questions
What is a co-ed prep school?
A co-ed prep school is a preparatory school shared by all genders. They learn side by side in the same classrooms, with the same curriculum and opportunities as one community.
Is Notting Hill Prep a co-ed prep school?
Yes. Notting Hill Prep is an independent school for children aged 4-13 of any gender, based in Notting Hill, West London.
What are the benefits of a co-ed prep school in London?
Co-education promotes confidence and empathy in children. As well as respect for their peers by learning alongside a mixed group every single day.
Is a co-ed prep school better than a single-sex prep school?
There is no blanket answer, it is something you must decide based on the social and educational needs of your child.
How does co-education prepare children for senior school?
Co-education prepares children for senior school and beyond by providing them with the skills to communicate, consider and respect all their fellow students. Helping them to form stronger friendships and working relationships.
What is the difference between co-ed and co-educational?
There is no difference at all, co-ed is merely an abbreviation of co-education.

Notting Hill Prep Philosophy
Notting Hill Prep or NHP, is an independent prep school in West London. We follow a ‘Thinking School’ Philosophy, combining traditional subjects with cognitive skills at all levels, to set children up for their academic future and beyond.
Notting Hill Prep was always intended to be a place where academic excellence never came before the joy of childhood. Instead, they work in tandem with both being treated as a priority for every child.
That belief is what motivates the following information on this page: our definition of a ‘Thinking School’, how metacognition looks day to day and the qualities we teach our pupils to enrich their understanding of their own learning. Habits we hope will exceed their time with us and continue to benefit them through their education and beyond.
What Is a Thinking School?
The term ‘Thinking School’ refers to an educational institution recognised and accredited by the University of Exeter for their work in the inclusion of cognitive learning strategies in their curriculum.
At Notting Hill Prep, we teach pupils to think critically, approach obstacles positively and learn habits that will remain with them for life. These principles are not treated as an add on or a bonus, they are a core part of school life and present in every lesson at NHP.
We have held Thinking School status for more than a decade and became the first prep school in England to become an Advanced Thinking School in 2021. An honour we were reaccredited with in 2024. The process is externally assessed and demands a school demonstrates an institution wide, consistent commitment to the approach, across all year groups and subjects.
This means all teachers and students share a universal learning language of thinking strategies.
As this framework is applied throughout the whole school, a child who learns these habits in reception will have them fully consolidated and at their disposal by the time they leave NHP.
Read more about our Thinking School approach.
What Is a Cognitive Curriculum?
Notting Hill Prep’s ‘cognitive curriculum’ is a combination of traditional academic learning and intentional teaching of thinking skills. Thought processes are viewed as a part of what we learn, helping pupils to truly understand what it is they’re taking in and become more adaptable learners.
This is evident in multiple aspects of our pupils’ development:
The NHP Habits
These refer to a set of behaviours and mindsets that students are encouraged to use throughout their school career. Academically, socially and in all parts of life, families often tell us this becomes a useful part of a household’s communication structure.
The NHP Habits include:
These habits are nurtured by teachers in all aspects of school life, deliberately named and drawn on to resolve social disagreements as well as academic problems. The goal is for this kind of language to become almost subconscious, it’s not uncommon to hear a young child at NHP praise a friend for their ‘perseverance’ or someone reflecting on what they’d do differently next time.
Cognitive Learning at NHP: From Classroom to Everyday Life
Our approach is not confined to lessons or subjects, it is woven into school life and community:
We think consistency is essential, with everyone following the same framework across the whole school. This is what allows the habits to genuinely become natural and lasting. Something they can use for the rest of their lives.

Why Families Choose NHP
When assessing which prep school is the perfect fit for your child, it’s about more than just academic results. The reasons people site when they explain choosing NHP go far beyond exam performance.
Browse where NHP students go on to study on our Leavers’ Destinations page.
Frequently Asked Questions
What is a Thinking School?
A thinking school refers to an institution that’s officially recognised for having cognitive development at the forefront of their educational approach. We have held accreditation from the University of Exeter since 2014 and Advanced Accreditation since 2021.
What are the NHP Habits?
These are the core principles that we aim to provide students with across all aspects of school life. These include curiosity, resilience, empathy, collaboration, independence, and reflection.
What is a cognitive curriculum?
This combines traditional academics with cognitive tools, giving pupils the ability not just to learn content but how to do so effectively.
What age groups follow the Thinking School curriculum at NHP?
Though complexity and development vary based on age. The ‘Thinking School’ approach is used across all age groups at Notting Hill Prep.
What makes NHP different from other prep schools?
We differentiate ourselves from other prep schools through our combination of academic excellence and our considered approach. We use cognitive learning strategies, pastoral care and the ‘thinking school’ methodology to prepare our pupils to succeed, not just to sit exams.
What Curriculum does NHP follow?
Pupils at Notting Hill Prep follow a diverse curriculum spanning both traditional and specialist subjects from reception to Year 8. With our thinking school approach incorporated throughout. You can find our full curriculum here.
What values are taught at Notting Hill Prep?
As well as setting children up for life academically we try to pass on values that will serve them well when they leave NHP. We hope they leave here ambitious, curious, self-aware, and considerate of others.

We don’t just teach children what to think. We teach them how.
Notting Hill Prep is proud to hold official Advanced Thinking School accreditation. A recognition awarded to institutions that promote thinking as a practiced skill rather than a secondary effect of a curriculum. Throughout their entire time with us at Notting Hill Prep, our students learn how to gather and evaluate their thoughts, weighing risks and reflecting on their own reasoning. Tools that can be applied both in school and beyond.
What “Thinking School” Actually Means
It’s easy to make claims about philosophy and approach to teaching. But to gain official recognition as a ‘Thinking School’ these must be substantiated and applied to everyday school life
The key idea that runs through all of this is referred to as Edward de Bono’s Six Thinking Hats. A simple framework that gives children the tools for their different ways of thinking, and the confidence to use each one intentionally depending on a learning scenario.
The Six Hats, in Plain English
Here is a quick guide for parents on what this entails, the six questions pupils are taught to ask themselves in every subject.
What’s my gut feeling?
What could go wrong?
Spotting flaws and risks
What’s the best case?
Finding value and benefits
What else is possible?
Generating new ideas
How are we thinking?
Planning and reflecting
See It in the Classroom
To further understand the ‘Thinking School’ you can see it in action. Here are some real examples of our philosophy in practice, exactly as your children will experience them.
Why It Matters
Thinking Schools accreditation isn’t merely a plaque or a buzz word. It’s a commitment to your child’s learning, giving them skills to reason, question and reflect. Tools that will help them in exams, interviews and in their life after their educational journey is complete.
Frequently Asked Questions
What are De Bono's Six Thinking Hats?
De Bono’s six thinking hats is a learning concept developed by Dr Edward de Bono that promotes approaching a problem from six different perspectives or ‘hats’. By ‘wearing’ one hat at a time, thinkers can isolate areas of thinking instead of mixing them all at once.
How does NHP teach thinking skills?
Thinking skills are applied daily in every lesson rather than taught on their own. Teachers allow challenging and questioning in class, encouraging children to consider their approaches from reception through to their final year. Pupils are given a framework that allows them to try things and make mistakes without fear, promoting confidence they can carry through their entire lives.
What does Thinking School accreditation mean?
Thinking School Accreditation means that Notting Hill Prep has been independently recognised for its application of thinking and learning strategies across all its teaching. This is awarded by the Cognitive Education Development Unit at the University of Exeter. We first achieved advanced status in 2014 and were reaccredited in 2024. We are the only prep school in the country to hold advanced status, reflecting our ethos and promise to both children and their parents.
